channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Speaker Raises Key Initiatives at CIS Parliamentary Assembly Meeting
item.description: Marlen Mamataliev, Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh, attended the 61st plenary session of the CIS Parliamentary Assembly in Turkmenistan. He delivered a report with proposals and shared initiatives to enhance relations. Mamataliev emphasized the Assembly's role in strengthening inter-state ties and parliamentary cooperation, and the need to expand economic ties among CIS member states.

item.title: Green Climate Fund to Allocate $2 Million to Tajikistan for Healthcare Sector
item.description: The Green Climate Fund, through the Asian Development Bank, will provide a $2 million grant to Tajikistan for a healthcare project. This agreement was reached during COP31 in Antalya, Turkey. The funds will support risk management related to glaciers and the 'Glaciers to Farmers' program, aiming to enhance climate change adaptation in the region.

item.title: Ukraine Reportedly Struck Crimea Bridge with Dutch Missiles; Russian Drone Crashed Near Dutch Embassy
item.description: Reports indicate Ukraine attacked the Crimea bridge using Dutch-made missiles. Ukrainian President Zelensky mentioned the use of Neptune missiles in the bridge attack, which are produced by a Dutch company. Two days after the attack, a drone crashed near the Dutch embassy building in Kyiv.

item.title: Kazakhstan Doubles Agricultural Product Exports, Reaching Nearly $7 Billion
item.description: Kazakhstan has doubled its agricultural product exports to nearly $7 billion, with processed products accounting for 52% of the total. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev noted a 28% increase in food production and the launch of 1,630 investment projects worth 2.7 trillion tenge. He emphasized the need to effectively utilize the sector's potential.

item.title: Kazakh President Orders Review of Rural Support Program Effectiveness
item.description: President Tokayev has instructed a review of the effectiveness of programs aimed at supporting rural areas. This directive comes amidst ongoing discussions about rural development and government initiatives. The review aims to assess the impact and efficiency of current support measures.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Mongolia to Expand Cooperation in Mining Sector
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ambassador to Mongolia, Aybek Moldogaziev, met with Mongolia's Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources, Gongo Gankhuyag. They discussed cooperation in geological exploration, digitalization of geological data, critical minerals research, and mineral raw material processing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enacts Law on Radioactive Waste Management and Safety
item.description: Uzbekistan has adopted a new law on radioactive waste, establishing a legal framework for managing radioactive waste. The law defines classifications, state policy principles, and responsibilities for handling radioactive materials, aiming to ensure safety for people and the environment.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Energy Sector Seeks $49 Billion in Investment
item.description: Kazakhstan's energy sector is looking for significant investment, with a reported need of $49 billion. The source asks who will be willing to make such substantial investments in the country's energy infrastructure.

item.title: Uzbekistan Forms Working Group to Address Greenhouse Farm Issues
item.description: A working group has been established in Uzbekistan's Tashkent region to study problems faced by greenhouse farms due to new environmental requirements. The group aims to find solutions enabling entrepreneurs to comply with regulations and continue operations.

item.title: Kazakhstan University Student Dies Amid Hazing Allegations; Officials Dismissed
item.description: A first-year student at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University has died, with relatives alleging pressure from senior students. Following the incident, the university's vice-rector and dean were dismissed, and staff on duty were suspended.

item.title: Chevrolet's Market Share in Uzbekistan Drops to 74 Percent Amidst Overall Sales Decline
item.description: Uzbekistan's new car sales fell 6.5% year-on-year in January-October, totaling 318,949 units. In October, sales decreased by 12% compared to the previous year, though they rose 6.3% from September. Chevrolet remains the market leader with 74% share, but this is down 7.8 percentage points from last year.

item.title: Kazakh President Addresses Third Forum of Agricultural Workers, Emphasizing Strategic Importance
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev addressed the third forum of agricultural workers, highlighting the sector's strategic importance to Kazakhstan's economy. He thanked participants for their contributions and noted that meaningful discussions were held on resource conservation, land use, and social conditions for rural workers. The government and relevant ministries are urged to consider these issues.

item.title: Jehovist-Ilyinist Sect Cell Discovered in Bishkek and Chuy Region
item.description: Seven individuals were detained in Bishkek and the Chuy region on suspicion of spreading the ideology of the banned religious organization 'Jehovists-Ilyinists' (Desnoy Bratstvo). Security services found religious literature and communication devices during searches. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Major Bank Privatization May Extend to 2028, Fitch Ratings Reports
item.description: Uzbekistan's plan to sell major state-owned banks, initially slated for 2027, may be delayed until 2028, according to Fitch Ratings. Banks require more time for preparation, and challenges with non-performing loans and currency risks persist. Fitch has upgraded the banking environment assessment to 'b+' stable.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan paves over 154 kilometers of roads in nine months
item.description: In nine months, Kyrgyzstan has asphalted over 154 kilometers of roads. The Ministry of Transport and Roads reported that the work is part of a plan to improve road infrastructure. The ministry aims to complete the remaining road construction projects by 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan will not agree to inflated prices in irrigation project talks with China, minister says
item.description: Uzbekistan's Minister of Water Management, Shavkat Khamrayev, stated that the country will not accept inflated prices in ongoing negotiations with Chinese companies for irrigation infrastructure reconstruction. He emphasized that while discussions continue, Uzbekistan prioritizes its national interests and will not agree to excessively high costs, even with Chinese investment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Measures to Protect Children from Violence at Global Conference
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Children's Rights Commissioner attended the second global conference on ending violence against children in Manila. The country presented three national commitments: integrating positive parenting programs in schools, developing school psychological services, and digitizing the child protection system for better inter-agency coordination and response.

item.title: Astana Investigates Scheme to Defraud Science Grants, Causing Nearly 300 Million Tenge Loss
item.description: Authorities in Astana are investigating a scheme to embezzle state grants for scientific research, resulting in a loss of over 297 million tenge. Two individuals have been detained. The scheme involved a grant for regenerating and purifying vegetable oils, with funds allegedly diverted through shell companies for non-existent equipment and services.

item.title: Mongolia's President Resigns Voluntarily for the First Time in History
item.description: Ukhnaagiin Khurelsukh has become the first president in Mongolia's history to resign voluntarily. The parliament accepted his resignation with 92.3% of votes. Parliamentary powers have been transferred to the Speaker of Parliament, Sandagiin Byambatsogt, who will serve until a new president is elected.

item.title: CIS Parliamentary Assembly Adopts Law Against Use of AI for Extremism
item.description: The CIS Parliamentary Assembly Council meeting in Turkmenistan adopted a law against the use of artificial intelligence for extremism. The Assembly's Chairman, Aybek Dadebay, highlighted the significance of the 1991 Almaty Declaration and the CIS's role in regional cooperation. He also informed about political reforms in Kazakhstan.

item.title: Uzbekistan-Turkey Business Council Holds Inaugural Meeting, Discusses Economic Cooperation
item.description: The first high-level meeting of the Uzbekistan-Turkey Business Support Council took place in Tashkent. Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz addressed the council, emphasizing the strengthening of economic ties. Mirziyoyev highlighted Uzbekistan's economic growth and investment goals, seeking enhanced cooperation with Turkey.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Eases Tax Payments with Digitalization and Increased Revenue Collection
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has collected over 338 billion soms in taxes in the first 10 months of 2026, funding infrastructure and development. Over the past five years, the tax system has seen significant digitalization, with most services moving online, reducing processing time from days to minutes. This has led to over 1.7 million users of online tax services and a substantial increase in budget revenues.

item.title: Kazakhstan Highlights Political Reforms at CIS Parliamentary Assembly Meeting in Turkmenistan
item.description: A delegation led by Kurultai Chairman Aybek Dadebay attended a CIS Parliamentary Assembly Council meeting in Turkmenistan. Dadebay spoke about Kazakhstan's ongoing political reforms initiated by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, emphasizing the goals of a Just, Strong, Clean, and Progressive Kazakhstan. He also noted the importance of the CIS as a platform for dialogue and cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Grants State Company Monopoly on International Internet Traffic
item.description: The Kyrgyz government has granted the state-owned company 'ElCat' exclusive rights as the sole operator for international internet traffic within the country. This move aims to strengthen digital sovereignty and state control over information flows. 'ElCat' will manage all international internet connections and transit, with other operators required to transfer their contracts.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Kylym Bank Signs Memorandum of Understanding with StoneX Group
item.description: Kylym Bank OJSC has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Singapore office of the international financial group StoneX Group. The agreement aims to develop cooperation, expand international financial transactions, and utilize modern financial instruments. Both parties expressed interest in leveraging StoneX Group's international financial infrastructure and expertise.

item.title: Kazakhstan Food Prices Surge Over 400% in Ten Years, Analysis Shows
item.description: A comparison of grocery receipts from ten years ago with current prices reveals a significant increase in food costs in Kazakhstan. A shopping basket that cost 13,347 tenge a decade ago now amounts to 59,302 tenge. The analysis examined average prices of staple foods and inflation dynamics over the past ten years.

item.title: Turkey's Anadolu Group Explores New Projects in Uzbekistan, Including Migros Expansion
item.description: Turkish conglomerate Anadolu Group is considering new projects in Uzbekistan, particularly involving its Migros supermarket chain. The company aims to expand its presence in retail, agriculture, food industry, and automotive sectors. They plan to combine Migros's retail and agri-business expertise with Uzbekistan's agricultural potential, though specific timelines and investment figures remain undisclosed.

item.title: Uzbekistan Police Arrest Gang for Nearly $100,000 Bank Card Fraud
item.description: In Nukus, Uzbekistan, a group of individuals has been arrested for allegedly stealing nearly one billion soms from bank cards. The suspects used malicious APK files distributed via Telegram to gain access to victims' accounts and transfer funds. The stolen money was used to purchase mobile phones, pay off online microloans, and fund online betting accounts. Police seized mobile devices and bank cards as part of the ongoing investigation.

item.title: CIS Financial Intelligence Heads Meet in Dushanbe to Combat Terrorism Financing
item.description: Dushanbe hosted the 33rd meeting of CIS heads of financial intelligence units on November 18, 2026. Participants discussed combating terrorism financing, fraud, drug trafficking, and illicit cryptocurrency use. Representatives from Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan attended, with Azerbaijan and Turkmenistan observing. The meeting emphasized the Council's role in addressing modern threats.

item.title: Kazakhstan Urged to Build Robust Investor Protection for Asset Tokenization
item.description: Kazakhstan must establish a strong citizen protection system for asset tokenization, including legal confirmation of rights, verification of existence and value, transparent issuers, and independent audits. Experts warn that without proper regulation, tokenization could lead to significant investor losses and become a channel for savings depletion.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission Replaces Four Local Council Deputies
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission has approved the early termination of powers for four local council deputies and updated the composition of territorial election commissions. New candidates have been assigned to fill the vacant mandates in various districts across the country.

item.title: World Bank mobilizes over $8.3 billion for Middle Corridor development
item.description: The World Bank Group is mobilizing over $8.3 billion in public and private funding to develop the Trans-Caspian transport corridor, known as the Middle Corridor. The development is projected to increase long-term employment in Kyrgyzstan by over 3% and boost GDP.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Reports Over 23,000 Domestic Violence Cases in Ten Months
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan, 23,414 cases of domestic violence were registered in ten months, a 28% increase from the previous year. Authorities issued 19,345 restraining orders, primarily against men. Women, men, and minors were among the 23,414 victims. Criminal cases and pre-trial proceedings were initiated for 535 incidents, including homicides and sexual assaults.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prepares for G20 Summit, Foreign Minister Holds European Meetings
item.description: Kazakhstan is preparing for the G20 summit in Miami, with President Tokayev discussing bilateral relations with the US. Foreign Minister Tileuberdi met with Austrian officials and the new SCO Secretary-General, and discussed trade and transport with European counterparts. The head of the National Security Committee was replaced following recent detentions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Open 74 Polling Stations Abroad for January 2027 Presidential Election
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will establish 74 polling stations in 33 countries for its citizens abroad participating in the January 27, 2027 presidential election. Russia will host the most stations (20), followed by Turkey and Kazakhstan (6 each). This number is lower than the 100 stations used in the 2025 elections.

item.title: Uzbekistan Inaugurates New Electrified Railway Line to Parkent
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched a new 24-kilometer electrified railway line connecting Baytkurgan to Parkent, costing 535.4 billion soums. The route, operational since September, features a new station and modern amenities on a six-car electric train. The journey from Tashkent to Parkent takes 1 hour 13 minutes and costs 10,000 soums.

item.title: Cattle Theft Ring Uncovered in Zhetysu Region, Nearly 600kg of Horse Meat Seized
item.description: Police in the Zhetysu region have detained two men suspected of a series of cattle thefts, involving 13 animals and causing nearly 10 million tenge in damages. The suspects allegedly stole cattle and horses, butchered them, and sold the meat in Taldykorgan. Approximately 600 kg of horse meat was seized.

item.title: Uzbekistan Ministry of Energy Clarifies AI-80 Gasoline Intended for Industrial Use
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Energy has clarified that AI-80 gasoline listed on the exchange is intended for industrial enterprises as raw material for further processing, not for retail sale to the public. Only licensed enterprises can purchase this fuel for production purposes, not for resale to motorists.

item.title: 95% of Saplings in Kyrgyzstan's Batken Region Project Died
item.description: Approximately 95% of saplings planted under the 'Green Border' project in Kyrgyzstan's Batken region have died. The Osh Environmental Prosecutor's Office discovered that project work was not fully completed, with inadequate conditions for growth and watering leading to mass plant death. A criminal case has been initiated.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Science Fund Embezzlement: Grant Funds Used for Cars
item.description: Kazakhstan's Financial Monitoring Agency has uncovered a scheme to embezzle state grants for commercializing scientific developments. A project monitor allegedly concealed violations for illegal reward. Funds intended for a plant regeneration project were diverted to purchase unsuitable equipment and personal vehicles, causing over 297 million tenge in state losses.
